title: 24-layer TiO2/SiO2 alternating stack with bounded thickness optimization for visible-NIR dichroic splitting
scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer alternating TiO2/SiO2 stack with individually optimized layer thicknesses (50-120 nm range) can achieve higher visible reflectance and NIR transmittance separation than a uniform quarter-wave DBR at 45 degrees incidence.
design_principle: Recalled knowledge: Dielectric mirrors work through constructive interference of reflections at each interface. Quarter-wave layers maximize reflectance at a design wavelength, but dichroic filters benefit from non-uniform thickness profiles that shape the reflection band edges. At 45 degrees, optical path length increases by 1/cos(refracted angle), shifting the effective quarter-wave condition. TiO2/SiO2 provides high index contrast (~2.4 vs ~1.45) for strong reflectance with fewer layers.
proposed_topology: 24 layers total, alternating TiO2/SiO2 starting with TiO2 on the incident side: TiO2/SiO2/TiO2/SiO2/TiO2/SiO2/TiO2/SiO2/TiO2/SiO2/TiO2/SiO2/TiO2/SiO2/TiO2/SiO2/TiO2/SiO2/TiO2/SiO2/TiO2/SiO2/TiO2/SiO2 on fused silica substrate
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers, bounded 50-120 nm
soft_objectives: maximize average reflectance in 450-650 nm band
maximize average transmittance in 700-1000 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: 24 layers is within typical sputtering/evaporation capability
thickness bounds 50-120 nm avoid extremely thin or thick layers that are difficult to control
TiO2 and SiO2 are standard coating materials with known deposition processes
theory_basis: Recalled: Quarter-wave optical thickness condition is n*d = lambda/4 for normal incidence, modified to n*d*cos(theta) = lambda/4 for oblique incidence
Recalled: High-low index contrast increases reflectance per pair, reducing required layer count
Recalled: Dichroic filters require band edge shaping beyond simple quarter-wave stacks
Recalled: 45 degree incidence introduces polarization splitting between s and p states
Recalled: TiO2 has higher absorption in UV but is transparent in visible-NIR range
expected_advantages: Alternating high-low index provides strong reflectance in visible band
Individual thickness optimization allows band edge tuning for better NIR transmission
24 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom for spectral shaping
known_risks: Uncertain whether fused silica substrate is in material registry - may need to use 'sio2' as substrate proxy
Recalled index values for TiO2 (~2.4) and SiO2 (~1.45) are approximate and wavelength-dependent
Polarization behavior at 45 degrees not fully characterized in my knowledge - s and p may split significantly
Thickness bounds 50-120 nm are chosen from memory of typical coating practice, not from specification
Would need to verify actual n/k dispersion data for both materials across 450-1000 nm range
Uncertain whether 24 layers is optimal or if fewer layers could achieve similar performance
execution_request_english: Design a 24-layer planar dielectric coating on fused silica substrate using alternating TiO2 (Siefke) and SiO2 (Gao) layers. Incident medium is air. Optimize all 24 layer thicknesses individually with bounds 50-120 nm per layer. Target: maximize reflectance in 450-650 nm wavelength band, maximize transmittance in 700-1000 nm wavelength band. Incidence angle is 45 degrees. Treat both s and p polarizations (unpolarized light). Use gradient-based thickness optimization. Material names: TiO2 (Siefke) for titanium dioxide, SiO2 (Gao) for silicon dioxide. Substrate: fused silica (use SiO2 (Gao) if fused silica not separately resolved). Maximum 24 layers fixed. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates count, tightest_margin, and final thicknesses_nm array.
revision_reason: Continuation of control arm with refined thickness bounds (50-120 nm) based on prior iteration feedback to prevent phase detuning from runaway layer growth while preserving the alternating TiO2/SiO2 topology and optimization approach
